$ apt update: Refreshes the list of software (which versions are available). Do it before apt install
$ apt upgrade: Updates installed software to new versions
$ apt -y: Answers "yes" automatically (does not ask for confirmation)
$ apt install -y: Answers "yes" automatically (does not ask for confirmation)
$ mkdir -p: Makes the folders along the way too. No error if it already exists
$ ls -l: Lists files in detail (permissions, size, date and time)
$ source: Loads a settings file into the current terminal (the same as .)
Loads a settings file into the current terminal (the same as source)
$ export: Sets an environment variable. Passed on to programs started from this terminal
$ echo: Shows text. With >> file name, appends to the end of the file
$ bash: Starts the shell (bash). -c runs the following string as a command
$ pwd: Shows where the current folder is
$ curl: Downloads data from a URL (also used to call web APIs)
$ curl -o: Sets the file name to save to
$ curl -fsSL: A shorthand for stop on errors, quiet, and follow redirects
$ wget: Downloads a file from a URL
$ grep: Finds lines containing text in files or output
$ grep -F: Searches for the text as it is, without regular expressions
$ awk: Splits lines and takes out chosen columns
$ dpkg: Handles Debian and Ubuntu packages (.deb) directly
$ locale: Shows the current language and character encoding settings
$ locale-gen: Makes language and character encoding settings (locales)
$ add-apt-repository: Adds a place (repository) where apt looks for software
$ add-apt-repository universe: Enables the software store managed by the Ubuntu community
$ usermod -aG: Adds the user to a group (-a adds, -G is group). Takes effect after logging in again
$ python3 -m: Runs a module as a program (python3 -m venv .venv and so on)
$ python3 -c: Runs the following string as Python code
$ python: Runs Python (the same as python3 inside a virtual environment)
$ venv: The module that makes Python virtual environments
$ .venv/bin/activate: The file that turns on the virtual environment. Load it with source
$ code: Opens VS Code. code . opens the current folder
Opens the current folder in VS Code
$ systemctl daemon-reload: Makes systemd reread service files after you change them
$ journalctl -f: Keeps showing new log lines as they come
$ git --recurse-submodules: Also fetches submodules (other repositories used inside)
$ git --branch: Chooses the branch (or tag) to fetch
$ git checkout: Switches to a branch or tag
$ g++: The C++ compiler (makes an executable from source)
$ g++ -Wall: Shows all warnings about common mistakes
$ g++ -o: Sets the name of the executable to make
